Title: CMAPSS Jet Engine Simulated Data
Author / Organization: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) / NASA Open Data Portal
Key Finding: The dataset contains multiple time series from simulated engines, with operating settings and sensor measurements. Training trajectories progress toward failure; test trajectories stop before failure and are used for remaining useful life (RUL) estimation.
Project Relevance: Primary candidate dataset for studying gradual engine degradation and developing/testing an AI wear-estimation model.
Limitation: Simulated engine data is not the same as real airline operational data. It does not include real spare-parts inventory, suppliers, or shipping records.

Title: Prognostics Center of Excellence Data Set Repository
Year: Web repository; check page for individual dataset dates
Key Finding: NASA's repository includes prognostics datasets, including turbofan engine degradation simulation data with sensor channels that characterize fault evolution.
Project Relevance: Provides an official place to find and cite degradation/prognostics data and supporting dataset descriptions.
Limitation: Not every dataset in the repository is aircraft-related; check the exact dataset and its access conditions before using it.

Title: Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation
Author / Organization: Abhinav Saxena, Kai Goebel, Don Simon, and Neil Eklund; listed by NASA
Key Finding: The paper describes a thermodynamic simulation that generates engine sensor time series as degradation progresses toward a failure criterion.
Project Relevance: Supports the background for studying gradual engine degradation from simulated sensor readings.
Limitation: It describes simulated damage progression; it does not validate our team's model or prove real-world maintenance outcomes.

Title: Predictive Maintenance Programs for Aircraft Engines Based on Remaining Useful Life Prediction
Author / Organization: Fei Xue, Guodong Jin, Lining Tan, Ye Yu, and Chengxi Zhang
Key Finding: The study examines predictive-maintenance approaches for aircraft engines using remaining useful life prediction and reports use of the NASA C-MAPSS dataset.
Project Relevance: Useful related work for explaining how RUL estimates can support maintenance planning.
Limitation: Its results belong to the paper's methods and experimental setup; they cannot be presented as results from our project.

Title: Aircraft Engine Prognostics Based on Informative Sensor Selection and Adaptive Degradation Modeling with Functional Principal Component Analysis
Author / Organization: Authors listed in the journal article
Key Finding: The article studies selecting informative engine sensors and modeling degradation using C-MAPSS simulated data to estimate future engine health.
Project Relevance: Supports researching sensor selection and tracking gradual changes in engine health over operating cycles.
Limitation: The reported results are specific to the paper's data and methods; real aircraft use would need separate validation.

Title: Alarm-Based Predictive Maintenance Scheduling for Aircraft Engines with Imperfect Remaining Useful Life Prognostics
Author / Organization: Ingeborg de Pater, Arthur Reijns, and Mihaela Mitici
Key Finding: The paper studies maintenance scheduling policies that use imperfect RUL predictions and analyzes maintenance-related costs.
Project Relevance: Connects wear/RUL estimates to a next-step maintenance planning decision rather than treating prediction as the final goal.
Limitation: The study's scheduling assumptions and cost model may differ from our simplified demonstration and do not replace approved maintenance procedures.

Title: Predictive Maintenance in Aircraft Engine Maintenance Using the C-MAPSS Dataset: Performance Comparison and Evaluation of Machine Learning Classification Algorithms
Key Finding: The study compares machine-learning and deep-learning approaches for a short-horizon aircraft-engine predictive-maintenance task using NASA C-MAPSS data.
Project Relevance: A recent reference for model choices, evaluation metrics, and the use of temporal patterns in engine sensor data.
Limitation: The paper frames its task as predicting failure within a defined number of cycles; that is not identical to our post-landing wear and parts-planning workflow.

Title: Spare Parts Management in the Aviation Maintenance Industry: A Literature Review
Author / Organization: Margarida Brito, Duarte Dinis, and Ana Barroso
Key Finding: The review discusses aviation spare-parts management, demand forecasting, and inventory planning to help reduce aircraft downtime caused by stockouts.
Project Relevance: Supports the supply-chain part of the project: translating maintenance needs into spare-parts planning.
Limitation: A literature review does not provide the team's actual inventory, supplier lead-time, or cost data.

Title: Sustainable Spare Parts Management in the Aviation Maintenance Industry: A Systematic Literature Review on Forecasting Approaches
Author / Organization: Authors listed on the journal article
Key Finding: The review discusses forecasting approaches for aviation spare-parts management, including the relationship between inventory planning, downtime, and resource use.
Project Relevance: Useful for discussing sustainability as a possible benefit of better planning and fewer avoidable urgent logistics movements.
Limitation: Do not claim this project reduces emissions unless the project measures or transparently estimates transport emissions; the article is not proof of our project's impact.

Title: ICAO Carbon Emissions Calculator
Year: Web tool; publication date not clearly shown on landing page
Key Finding: ICAO provides a calculator for estimating passenger air-travel carbon emissions based on trip information.
Project Relevance: Provides official aviation-emissions context, useful if the presentation discusses emissions methodology and boundaries.
Limitation: It estimates passenger flight emissions, not the emissions of shipping spare parts. It should not be used as a direct spare-parts transport-emissions calculator.
